item.title: Design and Iterative Development of Serious Exergames for Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder: Formative Multiple-Case Pilot Study
item.description: Background: Children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) exhibit cognitive, motor, and social difficulties that affect engagement, causing developmental delays, behavioral challenges, and obesity—interrelated concerns in daily functioning and well-being. item.title: Longitudinal Association Between Internet Gaming Disorder and School Refusal Among Adolescents Using a Random Intercept Cross-Lagged Panel Model: Three-Wave Prospective Cohort Study
item.description: Background: Internet gaming disorder (IGD) and school refusal are increasingly prevalent during adolescence, yet limited research has examined how they influence each other over time. Moreover, it is unclear whether the association differs by sex. Objective: This study aimed to investigate the within-person longitudinal associations between school refusal and IGD and potential sex differences in these associations among Chinese adolescent gamers. item.title: The Mechanism and Design Principles of Serious Games in Enhancing Adolescents’ Internet Adaptability
item.description: Adolescents’ internet adaptability (IA) is crucial for their online behavior and mental health. Serious games (SGs), as an emerging educational tool, hold promise for enhancing this adaptability through engaging, goal-oriented learning. Yet, direct evidence in this area remains limited. item.title: Home-Based Immersive Virtual Reality to Improve Motor Performance in Children and Adolescents With Developmental Coordination Disorder: Crossover Study
item.description: Background: Children with developmental coordination disorder (DCD) experience motor difficulties that limit daily activities and reduce physical activity enjoyment. Immersive virtual reality (VR) offers the potential for feedback-rich movement practice, but evidence for these effects in DCD remains limited. item.title: Feasibility and User Experience of Immersive Virtual Reality–Based Rehabilitation in Patients With Stroke: Single-Arm Pretest-Posttest Pilot Study
item.description: Background: Immersive virtual reality (VR) is promising in stroke rehabilitation; it is believed to promote motivation and intervention adherence among patients. However, existing work often lacks a structured assessment of user experience over a longer period of time. item.description: Background: Childhood and adolescent malnutrition, encompassing undernutrition and overnutrition, poses significant global health challenges, necessitating comprehensive dietary assessment tools. item.title: Game Elements in Military Trauma Care Education: Systematic Review
item.description: Background: Game elements may inform the design of both simulations and games. However, evidence on how individual game elements inform the design of military trauma training simulations and their educational purpose remains limited. Objective: This systematic review aimed to examine which game elements are used in the design of educational simulations for military trauma management, how they are implemented, for what purpose, and what outcomes are reported related to the game elements. item.title: The Effects of Dance-Based Exergaming on Mental Rotation, General Motor Coordination, and Math Achievement in Adolescent Students: Nonrandomized Controlled Pilot Study
item.description: Background: Exergaming can promote adolescent health by encouraging repetition of game-related tasks, potentially contributing to academic success by developing motor and cognitive skills. item.title: Effects of Virtual Nature Embodiment on Compassion, Empathy, Nature Connectedness, and Symptom Burden in Patients With Psychosis or Depression: An Explorative Clinical Study
item.description: Background: Nature experiences may have a positive impact on mental health. Innovative alternatives, such as immersive virtual reality (iVR), can have similar effects.
